item.title: Why Carney Isn’t Rushing Back to the Negotiating Table
item.description: Canadians back his tough stance on trade with the U.S. An expert says that support gives him little incentive to reopen talks soon.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney and his cabinet spent most of the week emphasizing efforts to build closer ties with other nations and plans for domestic infrastructure spending.

item.title: Visa Issue Threatens U.S.-Brazil Cooperation on Crime
item.description: Officials say the Trump administration is blocking some of Brazil’s efforts to expand cooperation on fighting transnational crime.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ionova and Edward Wong
item.media:credit: Mauricio Lima for The New York Times
item.media:description: Federal Revenue Service officers in Brazil setting up a drone for a flight in an area controlled by the agency in the Port of Santos this year.

item.title: Colombia to Start Aerial Spraying of Coca Crops Despite Health Worries
item.description: The plan — quickly challenged by a local court — came days after Colombia’s president and the U.S. secretary of state, Marco Rubio, discussed stronger measures against drug trafficking.
item.dc:creator: Genevieve Glatsky
item.media:description: An airplane spraying coca plants in El Catatumbo, a region in the Norte de Santander department of Colombia, in 2008.

item.title: Trump Administration Says U.S. Will Work With Peru on Crime Crackdown
item.description: The Trump administration is taking an increasingly militarized approach to Latin America, and it has pushed governments across the region to work with U.S. forces.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong and Mitra Taj
item.media:description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio during a news conference on Thursday in Peru’s capital, Lima, with the Peruvian president, Keiko Fujimori.

item.title: UK Sanctions Against Israeli Settlers Divide British Rabbis
item.description: Prominent rabbis reacted with a mix of support, condemnation and concern about the ramifications for Jews in Britain.
item.dc:creator: Amelia Nierenberg
item.media:credit: Ivor Prickett for The New York Times
item.media:description: An Israeli settler herding sheep in the West Bank and recording Palestinian villagers as they filmed him in July. International attention is focused on Israel’s expansion of illegal settlements there.

item.title: Ancient Tombs, Untouched by Looters, Are Found Under Peru’s Sands
item.description: One archaeologist called the tombs “the discovery of the decade” as the first burials from the Chimu kingdom to have escaped centuries of plunder.
item.dc:creator: Alan Yuhas

item.title: Carney, at a Cabinet Retreat, Considers Further Trade Strikes Against the U.S.
item.description: Canada’s retaliation this week against President Trump’s tariffs was met with more American tariffs and a closed U.S. border on some Canadian products.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada will consider whether to impose more tariffs against the United States during his cabinet retreat, which starts on Thursday.

item.title: Where to See the World’s Bayeux Tapestry Replicas
item.description: There are full-size replicas in a U.S. sports arena, an abbey in Denmark and a home in rural New Zealand. There’s even a more modest version for those who don’t like the original’s nudity.
item.dc:creator: Alex Marshall

item.title: Gander Welcomed Americans in 2001. Now, U.S.-Canada Tensions Hit Home.
item.description: The Newfoundland town welcomed thousands of frightened airline passengers on Sept. 11, but 25 years later, mixed emotions run through anniversary plans amid an escalating trade war.
item.dc:creator: Norimitsu Onishi and Renaud Philippe
item.media:credit: Renaud Philippe for The New York Times
item.media:description: A scene from the play Come From Away, performed in Gander, Newfoundland and Labrador. The musical tells the story of the 6,579 passengers and crew aboard 38 planes diverted to Gander after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks, and of the local residents who welcomed and cared for them.

item.title: U.S. Designates Ecuador’s Los Tiguerones Gang as Terrorist Group
item.description: The sanctions on Los Tiguerones imposed by Secretary of State Marco Rubio are an increasingly common U.S. tactic, though they will likely not hurt the gang’s finances.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong, Genevieve Glatsky and Annie Correal
item.media:description: The “Tiger Zone” graffiti in Guayaquil, Ecuador, refers to the gang that controls the sector.

item.title: Video Shows Grocery Store Manager Saving Toddler From Oncoming Traffic
item.description: Luis Cruz dashed into a busy street in Puebla, Mexico, to pull a girl out of the path of an approaching S.U.V. Footage of the rescue has made him a local sensation.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Wolfe

item.title: U.S. Takes Aim at New Target in Deadly Boat Strike Campaign
item.description: U.S. military officials in the past two weeks have sunk six large fishing vessels accused of providing fuel to fast boats carrying drugs from South America.
item.dc:creator: Annie Correal and Eric Schmitt
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: An image released by the U.S. military shows what it says is a floating refueling station being boarded last week. The Trump administration has said that refueling vessels support drug trafficking operations.

item.title: Canada’s Carney Doubles Down on Pivot Away from the United States
item.description: With tariffs on U.S. goods in effect and high-profile international engagements coming up, the Canadian leader keeps moving toward his goal.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff
item.media:credit: Justin Tang/The Canadian Press, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney, a former investment banker and central bank governor, is working to draw global investors to Canada.

item.title: At This Canadian Theater Festival, Forgiveness Is a Power Move
item.description: The outgoing artistic director of the Stratford Festival, Antoni Cimolino, directs “The Tempest,” and like Prospero, he understands how to wield acts of kindness.
item.dc:creator: Helen Shaw

item.title: Carney Says Retaliation Against U.S. Tariffs Was Unavoidable
item.description: In a video address, the prime minister said the United States was seeking “dependency, not a true economic partnership” from Canada.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:credit: Justin Tang/The Canadian Press, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Tuesday that American trade negotiators were seeking Canadian dependency, not partnership.

item.title: Bombardier Shares Down as Trump’s Trade War Targets Canadian Jet Maker
item.description: The Montreal-based company’s share price dropped after President Trump threatened to bar it from selling in the United States.
item.dc:creator: John Yoon
item.media:description: Planes in production on the factory floor at a Bombardier plant in Mississauga, Ontario, in 2024.

item.title: Rubio Meets Colombia’s Leader, Cites Progress on Security and Tariffs
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he would talk with leaders in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru this week about drug-traffickers and trade deals.
item.dc:creator: Annie Correal and Genevieve Glatsky
item.media:credit: Pete Marovich for The New York Times
item.media:description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaking at a cabinet meeting last week.

item.title: Nazi-Looted Painting in Real Estate Listing Must Be Returned
item.description: The 18th-century painting “Portrait of a Lady” was stolen by a high-ranking Nazi in the 1940s. Last year, it surfaced in a real estate listing in Argentina.
item.dc:creator: Claire Moses
item.media:description: Ariel Bassano, a visual arts teacher, left, standing next to the painting “Portrait of a Lady” at the public prosecutor’s office in Mar del Plata, Argentina. The 18th-century work had been missing for eight decades.

item.title: Canada’s Retaliatory Tariffs Set to Take Effect as Trump Threatens to Escalate
item.description: New Canadian levies of up to 50 percent are expected to begin Tuesday, even as Washington warns of a new round of American tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: The Blue Water Bridge, connecting Sarnia, Ontario, and Port Huron, Mich., this month.

item.title: In Peru, the Trump Administration Sees the Limits of Its Anti-China Push
item.description: As Secretary of State Marco Rubio travels this week to Peru, its growing economic ties to China have raised tensions with the U.S., but show no signs of reversing course.
item.dc:creator: Genevieve Glatsky and Sara Wayra
item.media:credit: Sara Wayra for The New York Times
item.media:description: The enormous new Chinese-operated cargo port at Chancay, Peru, is a source of tension with Washington, but Peruvians see it as economically vital.

item.title: Haitians Deported From U.S. Are Left Broke and Stranded
item.description: Hundreds have been deported to Haiti in recent weeks, and some say they have been left with no money, no protection from gangs and no place to go.
item.dc:creator: Frances Robles
item.media:description: Reginald Dorvilma, 36, who was arrested in Orlando, Fla., two months ago and arrived in Haiti on Thursday.

item.title: A Bad Year for Bees Gets Worse as Trump’s Tariffs Hit Canada’s Honey Belt
item.description: Alberta produces 40 percent of Canada’s honey. This year, rain and President Trump’s trade war have combined to threaten the industry.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai and Todd Korol

item.title: U.S. Military Sinks Boats Said to Aid Drug Smuggling Near Ecuador
item.description: Unlike dozens of similar strikes, no one was killed after people suspected of drug smuggling were removed from what the U.S. military described as a floating refueling station.
item.dc:creator: John Ismay
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Fishermen made their way to the ocean along Ecuador’s coast, in June.
